bodyHtml:
Back to Works & Blog
BLENDER 5.3 / 3DGS / VFX · 2026-09-19

Native 3DGS in Blender 5.3:
performance and VFX output on a 17.2M-splat scan

Blender now imports PLY splats without an add-on and renders them in EEVEE and Cycles.
I measured the speed on real data and checked how far it goes as compositing material.

I'm Kou Nakamura from Locahun 3D.
Blender 5.3 handles 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) natively, with no add-on.
It imports PLY and SPZ and renders splats in Workbench, EEVEE and Cycles.
5.3 is in alpha now; the stable release is planned for November 10.
I tested performance and VFX use with a full 17.2-million-splat scan of Shibuya Scramble Crossing.

Tested on an alpha buildI used the official daily build (5.3.0 Alpha, September 18, 2026).
Behavior and numbers may change before the stable release.

01 Importing a PLY gives you 3DGS directly

Choose a PLY or SPZ from File > Import and it arrives as a Point Cloud object.
Its type is "3D Gaussian Splats", and every splat carries these attributes.

AttributeContent
positionContentPosition
scaleContentSize
rotationContentOrientation (quaternion)
radiance:baseContentBase color and opacity
radiance:sh_0…ContentSpherical harmonics (view-dependent color)

Spherical harmonics up to degree 3 (45 coefficients) are imported and rendered.
Coordinates are converted to Blender's orientation, so the scene lands Z-up.
Delete Geometry in Geometry Nodes crops a region while keeping it 3DGS.
The Set Point Cloud Type node switches between splats and plain points.

02 Test setup

ItemDetail
BlenderDetail5.3.0 Alpha (main.1a542e41319f / 2026-09-18)
GPUDetailRTX 5090 32GB / driver 610.47
DataDetailShibuya Scramble PLY / 17,201,445 splats / 1.17GB
SubsetsDetailEvenly thinned 100K, 1M and 4M splats
OutputDetail1920×1080 / 64 samples / Cycles without denoising

Figures are medians of three runs.
The first render includes shader preparation and is listed separately.

03 About two seconds per frame at 17.2M splats

SplatsImportEEVEE (first / after)Cycles GPU (first / after)
100KImport0.01sEEVEE (first / after)0.69 / 0.19sCycles GPU (first / after)1.26 / 0.48s
1MImport0.08sEEVEE (first / after)0.75 / 0.32sCycles GPU (first / after)0.80 / 0.65s
4MImport0.31sEEVEE (first / after)1.08 / 0.59sCycles GPU (first / after)1.23 / 1.04s
17.2MImport1.6sEEVEE (first / after)2.41 / 1.73sCycles GPU (first / after)2.78 / 2.57s
SplatsPeak RAM (EEVEE / Cycles)Added VRAM (EEVEE / Cycles)
1MPeak RAM (EEVEE / Cycles)1.0 / 0.8GBAdded VRAM (EEVEE / Cycles)+1.6 / +3.5GB
17.2MPeak RAM (EEVEE / Cycles)3.2 / 3.0GBAdded VRAM (EEVEE / Cycles)+4.5 / +4.9GB

A 24-frame camera move renders at 1.52s per frame in EEVEE and 2.47s in Cycles.
The 17.2M-splat .blend is 919MB; it saves in 0.34s and reopens in 0.6s.
The release notes say performance is not ideal yet, but on this machine it is practical.
Results will differ on weaker GPUs or on data with many spherical harmonics.

Thinned data shows gaps between splats, so use the full scan for production.

04 Compositing basics work as they are

FeatureEEVEECyclesUse
Transparent backgroundEEVEE○Cycles○UseHand off with alpha
Occlusion with CGEEVEE○Cycles○UseForeground CG layers correctly
HoldoutEEVEE○Cycles○UseCut splats out with CG
Shadow catcherEEVEE—Cycles○UseExtract CG shadows only
Depth of fieldEEVEE○Cycles○UseApply at render time
Motion blurEEVEE○Cycles△UseCycles produced ghosting with these settings
Depth / Normal passesEEVEE△Cycles△UseValues exist, with holes and noise
Mist / Position / Vector / CryptomatteEEVEE○Cycles○UseValues are written

05 Four things that stop production use

Lights have no effect

Splats render as emissive material, with the capture lighting baked into their color.
A strong light does not change the splat color at all.
Splats do not receive CG shadows either.
Match your CG lighting to the direction of the captured light.
Relighting the background, such as turning it into night, is not possible.

The depth pass has holes

7.5–8.4% of splat pixels have no depth value.
Semi-transparent splats leave the depth at infinity.
Depth-based fog or post depth of field gets noisy, so apply depth of field at render time.
Normals are not coherent enough for relighting either.

Export drops the color

PLY export writes a file with zero splats.
USD keeps position, scale and rotation but loses color and opacity.
You cannot pass 3DGS to Houdini or Nuke as-is; render in Blender and deliver EXRs.

Apply Transform breaks the look

After matchmoving, keep the object transform and do not apply it.

Write one EXR per passIn this alpha, a multilayer EXR only contains Combined.
Mesh-only scenes behave the same, so this is not a 3DGS issue.
Use the compositor File Output node with one EXR per pass to get depth and normals.

06 Start with background plates and previs

UseFit
Replacing live-action backgrounds with 3DGSFit◎ Quality and speed are sufficient
CG in front of a 3DGS backgroundFit○ Match lighting on the CG side
Previs, location scouting, camera workFit◎ Fast import, light to handle
Relighting the backgroundFit× Not possible
Depth-based post processingFit△ Noisy
Passing 3DGS to other softwareFit× Color is lost

Blender 5.3's 3DGS support is already practical for importing, moving a camera and rendering images.
Three walls remain: no lighting response, holes in depth, and color lost on export.
Start with background plates and previs, and composite CG with the shadow catcher and one-EXR-per-pass output.
I will revisit SPZ import and real spherical-harmonics data after the stable release.
